source.title: The Dynamic of Consensus in Deep Networks and the Identification of Noisy Labels
source.authors: Daniel Shwartz; Uri Stern; Daphna Weinshall

record.tranche_reason: Tests the timing of learning clean and noisy labels in deep network ensembles using agreement and distribution measures, rather than directly reproducing the original memorization measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses fitting noisy and random labels, but those statements cite prior work. Its own relevant results concern the timing and cross-network consistency of learning clean versus noisy examples. Performance numbers for DisagreeNet are not results about the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own clean-versus-noisy learning trajectories: clean examples predominate in early learning, while noisy-label memorization predominates later. Its ensemble agreement analyses also measure differences in how clean and noisy labels are learned, bearing on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors find greater variability across networks in when noisy examples are learned, and use this observation to identify noisy labels, estimate noise levels and improve classification after filtration.
record.recipe_differences: Studies ensemble agreement dynamics and noisy-label identification, rather than directly testing memorization of fully random labels or the original training-error and test-error measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The BI decline is reported when overfit occurs; the authors state that the predicted BI decrease is not observed when overfit does not occur. The clean/noisy separation is less pronounced with symmetric noise than with asymmetric noise, as described in Appendix G.

fits_no_version.finding: BI decreases with falling test accuracy when overfit occurs; this relationship is not observed when overfit does not occur.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Declining ensemble agreement can indicate overfitting during noisy-label training.

record.problems: The claim-relevant dynamics are described qualitatively and often presented in figures without numeric values in the text. The reported experiment uses an ensemble and noisy-label settings, so it does not establish the broader random-label fitting claim.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were omitted. DisagreeNet filtration, noise-estimation, and retraining-accuracy results were excluded because they evaluate the proposed method rather than the claim’s predicted behavior.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence time as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit together with steadily increasing test error across the full corruption range. Accuracy after filtration and retraining does not test this.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms true-label generalization. The augmentation ablation measures filtration performance.
Direct identification of shared features learned before memorization, and learning trajectories on a completely randomly labeled dataset.

missing.what: Appendix G analyzes clean and noisy subsets selected to have approximately equal learning times in one network. Their subsequent ensemble agreement rises differently, providing additional evidence about distinct learning dynamics and documenting overlap in individual-network learning times. Separate this behavioral result from ELP-versus-confidence filtration comparisons.
missing.locator: Appendix G, Figure 10; 20% and 40% symmetric and asymmetric noise

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text supports qualitative conclusions without readable numerical trajectories. Neither failure of BI to decline nor weaker filtration performance establishes failure of V6. No verdict is based on the proposed method's benchmark performance.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks reach zero or near-zero error on completely random labels, and whether test error is at chance.
Training-time cost relative to true labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steady test-error change across corruption fractions.
Whether regularization or augmentation prevents random-label fitting or is necessary for true-label generalization.
Does not compare a single network’s learning of real and random labels, or establish the full pattern across training methods and datasets.

rows.subject: 10 DenseNet networks
rows.operation_detail: Measured the Bimodality Index (BI) of ensemble predictions over epochs during training with noisy labels.
rows.measure: BI over epochs; the authors describe an initial rise during learning and a possible subsequent decline as noisy-example memorization dominates.
rows.value: The text describes most clean examples as being learned in the initial phase and noisy-example memorization as dominating the later phase.
rows.note: Qualitative result described alongside the figure; the text does not give numeric BI values.
rows.check: The qualitative value is supported by Section 3.2 and Figure 2a. The evidence for V6 is the clean/noisy TPA trajectories and their stated temporal ordering; a rise or decline in BI alone would not establish that ordering.

rows.subject: ensemble of deep networks
rows.operation_detail: Compared empirical inter-network agreement distributions for clean and noisy examples with matched binomial distributions over epochs.

conditions.value: clean and noisy examples analyzed separately

rows.measure: Wasserstein distance between the agreement distribution and matched binomial distribution.
rows.value: The clean-example distribution is described as far from binomial; the noisy-example distribution is described as much closer.
rows.note: Qualitative comparison described in the appendix; no numeric distances are stated in the text.
rows.check: Appendix B supports different learning dynamics: noisy-example agreement is closer to matched binomial distributions, indicating less synchronized memorization across networks. This does not independently establish that noisy labels are learned later. Dataset, architecture, ensemble size and noise condition are unspecified in this appendix.

relationships.condition: Ten independently trained DenseNets on CIFAR-10 with 20% symmetric label noise
relationships.reason: R1 reports that most clean examples are learned during the initial phase and noisy-example memorization dominates the later phase.
relationships.display_finding: Most clean examples were learned during the initial phase, while noisy-example memorization dominated the later phase.

relationships.condition: Clean and noisy subsets in the Appendix B ensemble analysis; experimental configuration unspecified
relationships.reason: R2 shows different learning dynamics: noisy-label memorization is less synchronized across networks than clean-label learning; this supports the dynamics component of V6.
relationships.display_finding: Noisy-label memorization was less synchronized across networks than clean-label learning.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Clean and noisy examples in the reported ensemble learning-dynamics analyses
reader_labels.reason: The reported results describe clean examples as learned in the earlier phase and noisy-example learning as less synchronized across models (R1, R2).
